title: Moab
lead: A kingdom on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, traced in Genesis to Lot's son Moab. Moab was often Israel's enemy, yet it was the home of Ruth, David's great-grandmother, and a place of refuge for David's parents.

sections.b: Genesis traces Moab to Lot and his older daughter (Genesis 19:30–38). Moab's king Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel (Numbers 22–24), and Israel sinned with Moabite women at Peor (Numbers 25). Deuteronomy bars Moabites from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:3–6), yet forbids Israel to take Moab's land (Deuteronomy 2:9). The Moabite king Eglon ruled Israel until Ehud killed him (Judges 3:12–30). David conquered Moab (2 Samuel 8:2), and King Mesha rebelled after Ahab's death (2 Kings 3), a war the Mesha Stele tells from Moab's side. The prophets pronounce judgment on Moab (Isaiah 15–16; Jeremiah 48), but Jeremiah ends with a promise: "I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the last days" (Jeremiah 48:47).
